scenes.visual: Title 'One touch, several signals' over a hand stroking a forearm, drawn as a simple line sketch.

scenes.tts: A light touch on your skin is not one signal. Several kinds of touch neuron report it at once, and each kind reports a different part. Some fire while the skin moves. Some keep firing through a steady press, and mark its edges. Some are most sensitive to fast vibration. Some catch the slightest bend of a hair. And some, very slow, answer a gentle stroke. Each kind is a low threshold mechano receptor, or L T M R.

scenes.visual: One fingertip touches skin; five coloured traces split off beneath it, each labelled by feature: motion, steady press and edges, vibration, hair bend, gentle stroke. The label LTMR appears.

scenes.tts: Each class has its own ending, speed and time course. Merkel endings serve the steady press. Pa sinny an corpuscles serve vibration. At mouse hairs, A beta R A neurons conduct at thirteen point six metres per second, A delta neurons at five point eight, and C neurons at zero point five eight, by far the slowest. So one touch reaches the spinal cord as several signals, at several speeds.

scenes.tts: These classes can share one hair. On a mouse's back, the awl aw keen hair is fenced by lan see oh late endings from three classes: A beta R A, A delta and C. Each ending is an axon branch running along the follicle, like a picket in a fence, with terminal Schwann cells between the pickets. Most hairs are also wrapped by the ending of one more class, the field L T M R.

scenes.visual: A follicle with three colours of pickets fades in; purple Schwann cell blobs appear between them; a fourth colour wraps around the follicle as a ring labelled field-LTMR.

scenes.tts: How did anyone learn which endings belong to which neurons? Li and colleagues labelled the C, A delta and A beta R A classes genetically, and checked each label by recording. A label is only a handle until physiology confirms it. Then they imaged whole mounts of mouse trunk skin. Guard hairs carry A beta R A endings, plus S A one endings in a touch dome beside the hair. Awl aw keen hairs carry A beta R A, A delta, and C. Zigzag hairs carry A delta and C. The same combinations repeat across the skin.
scenes.caption: How did anyone learn which endings belong to which neurons? Li and colleagues labelled the C, Aδ and Aβ RA classes genetically, and checked each label by recording. A label is only a handle until physiology confirms it. Then they imaged whole mounts of mouse trunk skin. Guard hairs carry Aβ RA endings, plus SA1 endings in a touch dome beside the hair. Awl aw keen hairs carry Aβ RA, Aδ, and C. Zigzag hairs carry Aδ and C. The same combinations repeat across the skin.
scenes.visual: Three steps (label, record, image) chain across; then the three hair types appear side by side, each with its own mix of coloured pickets, and the trio tiles across a patch of skin.

scenes.tts: Your own skin has counterparts of some of these classes. Recording single nerve fibres in awake volunteers, a method called micro neur ography, sorts human touch afferents by how they fire. In hairy skin it found slow, unmyelinated afferents that respond to gentle stroking. These C tactile afferents behave like mouse C L T M Rs. Reviews conclude that they support gentle, affective touch, the social side of touch. But not every affective touch depends on them.

Reviews conclude that they support gentle, affective touch, the social side of touch. But not every affective touch depends on them.
scenes.visual: A fine electrode enters a forearm nerve; a slow spike train appears as a hand strokes the forearm; the label 'C-tactile: affective touch' appears with a small 'not the only route' note.

scenes.tts: So why build a sense this way? Because no single class reports a whole touch. In one model, a poke at one spot drives mostly the Merkel endings beside a guard hair, and a stroke across the fur drives a different mix. The nervous system reads the combination, as the signals arrive at different speeds. One caution when you count endings. A single neuron branches to many hairs. So endings at a hair are not a count of neurons.
